pr_title: Added example of how to change sprite at runtime
pr_body:
# Objective

Fixes: https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/issues/3130

## Solution

- Added an example on how to update sprites at runtime
- Showing an example of how to alter the color value
- Showing an example of how to swap the texture
pr_comments:
Thanks for making this! So, the other thing you can actually do is fetch the `Res<Assets<ColorMaterial>>`, and then *modify* the underlying asset using `Assets::get_mut` or `Assets::set`. This will then update all of the entities that are using that handle.

This is a subtly distinct but powerful tool (especially when working with more tweakable assets like meshes). Understanding this distinction is really what made the assets system click for me when I was first learning, so I think it's valuable to highlight :)

The other question is where do we want this example to live. I had originally envisioned two examples, one for 2D and one for 3D. After chewing on it for a bit, I think this is fundamentally an *assets* example since we're trying to explain the subtleties of the assets and handles model, and the duplication would be redundant. Do you agree with my assessment there?

issue_context.title: Examples to demonstrate changing a sprite and texture
issue_context.body:
## How can Bevy's documentation be improved?

Newcomers are often a bit lost when trying to learn how to idiomatically work with assets and handles.

The most common stumbling block is "how do I change a sprite once loaded?".

We should add two sibling examples, one for sprites, and one for meshes:

- show how to query for sprite / mesh handles, and change what they point to
- show how to programatically change the properties of a sprite / mesh (e.g. color, reflectance, translucency or so on)
- show how to mutate the underlying asset to e.g. add more vertexes
comments: This looks like good learning material for me, I'll pick this up.
Awesome. https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/pull/15056 gets into the strategies a little bit, but it would be very nice to have a hands-on example or two.
This is possibly an obvious question, but do we mean an example for `Mesh2d` or `Mesh` here?
Either is fine: I think `Mesh` is more common.
